scores.evidence: Respect GitHub API rate limits (5000 requests/hour)
scores.rationale: Uses a fixed 5000/hr figure that doesn't fit GitHub App installation tokens, suggests "OAuth token management", and uses an unsupported vector similarity > 0.95 as a reliable duplicate-close signal; it also treats "Sanitize code generation outputs" as a security control.

scores.evidence: Create pull requests for simple fixes
scores.rationale: It is mostly a triage bot. The resolution part is a decision tree of comments and suggestions with no reproduce, fix or verify loop, so the resolve half of the request is barely met.

scores.evidence: Event Listener ──→ Analysis Engine ──→ Resolution Engine
scores.rationale: The block diagram is recognizable, but the Triage Module, Knowledge Base and Memory module overlap and own data unclearly. The Resolution Engine auto-closes while the Safety section says to escalate edge cases.

It gives target numbers like >95% accuracy with no basis and no offline evaluation against historical issues. The only risk-specific note is "Start with read-only actions", which is not a real validation plan.
Assumptions about scale, team, repos and stack are not stated. Invented targets such as 99.9% uptime and 4.5/5 satisfaction are presented as fact.

scores.evidence: Rate limit agent to prevent spam
scores.rationale: Failure modes appear only as generic safety bullets. Prompt injection, partial failures, duplicate webhook delivery, loops and sandbox escape are missing.
It names tools, but there is no rollback, ownership, incident response, alerting signal design or change process.
Model inference cost, token budgets and cost per issue are not discussed. Pinecone, Kubernetes and the Claude/GPT-4 calls are chosen with no cost reasoning.
Reversibility is not discussed. Vendors are listed as alternatives, but Pinecone, Jira, Datadog and Confluence are coupled with no isolation or exit paths.
It stacks Celery, Redis, Postgres, Pinecone, Kubernetes, trained ML models, sentiment analysis, translation and many integrations with no stated need. It also lacks essentials such as a sandbox.
The phases are a high-level list with no dependency reasoning, no checkable intermediate results and no concrete first steps. The closing steps are generic.

checklist.evidence: Start with read-only actions before automation
Collect training data from historical issues
Always add comment explaining automatic action
Rate limit agent to prevent spam
Maintain audit log of all agent decisions
Code Context: Repository structure, recent changes
Event Queue: Process events asynchronously with priority queue

traps.evidence: Create pull requests for simple fixes
Analyze this GitHub issue: - Title: {title} - Description: {description}
Stale with no response (30+ days, non-critical)
Rate limit agent to prevent spam

note: A generic, buzzword-heavy triage bot. It auto-closes on raw similarity thresholds and ignores prompt injection, sandboxing, fix verification, cost budgets and loop control.
